title: Halakhah
notes: Cited for: halakhah, 'the Way', regulates religious observance and daily conduct; developed through the Mishnah (early 3rd century) and Talmud; Conservative rabbis adapt some laws, Reform Jews do not treat most as binding.

title: Canon law
notes: Cited for: canon law made by church authority in the Catholic, Orthodox, independent Eastern and Anglican churches; it governs church life, not the state; it influenced secular marriage law and criminal procedure.

title: Code of Canon Law, Book I: General Norms (canons 7-22)
notes: Cited for: canon 11, merely ecclesiastical laws bind those baptized in or received into the Catholic Church.

title: Islamic calendar
notes: Cited for: purely lunar year of 12 months and 354 or 355 days with no leap months; Ramadan the ninth month; months retrogress through the seasons in about 32.5 years.

title: Jewish religious year
notes: Cited for: lunisolar calendar; leap month (First Adar) seven times in 19 years so festivals stay in season; Passover from 15 Nisan.

title: Hindu calendar
notes: Cited for: 12 lunar months of about 354 days reconciled with the solar year by intercalation; most major festivals shift against the Gregorian calendar.

title: Diwali
notes: Cited for: Diwali centers on the new moon of the lunar month Karttika, in late October or November.

title: Easter
notes: Cited for: Easter on the first Sunday after the first full moon on or after March 21; falls between March 22 and April 25.

title: Kashruth
notes: Cited for: permitted animals (cud and cloven hoof; fins and scales, so no shellfish); strict separation of meat and dairy; for observant Jews no motive needed beyond God's command; rules from Leviticus and Deuteronomy.

title: Halal
notes: Cited for: halal permitted, haram forbidden; pork, alcohol, blood and carrion prohibited; slaughterer invokes God's name; rules from the Quran and Hadith.

title: Vegetarianism
notes: Cited for: ideal of not harming sentient creatures taken up in Hinduism and applied especially to the cow.

title: Religion in India: Tolerance and Segregation, chapter 8: Religion and food
notes: Cited for: 44% of Hindus and 92% of Jains in India say they are vegetarian; 67% of Jains abstain from root vegetables because uprooting destroys the plant; most Hindus say a person who eats beef cannot be Hindu.

title: Are All Buddhists Vegetarians?
notes: Cited for: first precept to refrain from taking life; early monastics ate the alms they were given but not animals slaughtered for them; vegetarianism the norm in Chinese, Korean and Vietnamese monasteries and a personal choice in Theravada and Tibetan Buddhism.

title: Judaism: Art and iconography
notes: Cited for: the Second Commandment aimed at idol worship; 3rd-century Dura-Europos synagogue painted with biblical scenes.

title: Why are images of Muhammad generally prohibited in Islam?
notes: Cited for: Muslims reject images of the Prophet as a form of idolatry inconsistent with monotheism; aniconism an early feature of Islam.

title: Islam: Religion and the arts
notes: Cited for: aniconism rests on the belief that God is the sole author of life; the arabesque spiritually represents the infinite vastness of God.

title: Pillars of Islam
notes: Cited for: zakat of one-fortieth of cash and savings above the nisab; those below it exempt; recipients defined in the ninth sura.

title: zakat (glossary)
notes: Cited for: zakat literally means 'purification'; about 2.5 percent of accumulated wealth.

title: Maimonides' Ladder of Tzedakah
notes: Cited for: tzedakah as justice and righteousness; Maimonides' highest degree (gift, loan or partnership that strengthens the poor person's hand), then anonymous giving; Mishneh Torah, Gifts to the Poor 10:7-14.

title: Mishne Torah
notes: Cited for: Maimonides' code of Jewish law, composed in the 12th century.

title: Dana (Buddhism)
notes: Cited for: dana, gift-giving, such as food and robes for monks or gifts to temples, builds merit that Buddhists believe improves karma and rebirth.

title: Langar
notes: Cited for: communal refectory of a gurdwara serving vegetarian food to all; everyone sits in a straight line, neither ahead nor behind; originated as a protest against the caste system; Sikh principle of selfless service and equality.

title: Caste (social differentiation)
notes: Cited for: four varnas traced to a hymn in the Rigveda; jatis endogamous and tied to hereditary occupations; those handling impure substances treated as untouchable; untouchability declared unlawful in the constitution adopted 1949-50.

title: Dalit
notes: Cited for: Dalit refers to groups historically marginalized in Hindu caste society; members of the Scheduled Castes often prefer the term.

title: Vasala Sutta: Discourse on Outcasts (Sutta Nipata 1.7), translated by Piyadassi Thera
notes: Cited for: the Buddha's teaching that one is not an outcast or a brahman by birth but by deeds.

title: Ravidas
notes: Cited for: bhakti poet born into the leatherworking Chamar community, considered untouchable; 'all are made from the same clay'; about 40 poems in the Adi Granth.

title: Arya Samaj
notes: Cited for: founded 1875 by Dayananda Sarasvati; opposed basing caste on birth rather than merit; rejected untouchability.

title: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar
notes: Cited for: born into a Dalit Mahar family; chaired the constitution's drafting committee; in October 1956, in despair at untouchability's perpetuation in Hindu doctrine, became a Buddhist with about 200,000 Dalits at Nagpur.

title: Constitution of India
notes: Cited for: adopted 26 November 1949, in effect 26 January 1950; Article 15 bans discrimination based on caste; Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

title: Ahimsa
notes: Cited for: ahimsa, not causing harm to living things, in Jainism, Hinduism and Buddhism; paramount in Jainism, extending to insects, plants, microbes and thoughts; less strict in Hinduism and Buddhism; Gandhi built satyagraha on it.

title: Mahatma Gandhi
notes: Cited for: Gandhi grew up in a home with a strong tinge of Jainism and embraced ahimsa, vegetarianism and fasting for self-purification.

title: Satyagraha
notes: Cited for: satyagraha, 'holding onto truth', conceived by Gandhi in 1906 in the Transvaal; drew on ahimsa, Hindu and biblical texts, Tolstoy and Thoreau; Salt March of 1930; influence on King.

title: Gandhi, Mohandas K.
publisher: The Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford University
notes: Cited for: King met Gandhian ideas at Crozer; heard Mordecai Johnson in 1950; first used nonviolent direct action in the Montgomery bus boycott; five-week trip to India in 1959.

title: Nonviolence
publisher: The Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford University
notes: Cited for: 'Christ furnished the spirit and motivation while Gandhi furnished the method'; agape as the motive of nonviolence.

title: Martin Luther King, Jr.
notes: Cited for: Baptist minister at Dexter Avenue Baptist Church in Montgomery; met Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolence at Crozer Theological Seminary.

title: Spanish Inquisition
notes: Cited for: on March 31, 1492, Ferdinand and Isabella gave Spanish Jews the choice of exile or baptism; more than 160,000 were expelled.

title: Introduction to the Holocaust
notes: Cited for: the Holocaust was the systematic, state-sponsored persecution and murder of six million European Jews by the Nazi German regime and its allies and collaborators, 1933 to 1945.

title: Iran: UN experts alarmed by escalating religious persecution
publisher: United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
notes: Cited for: August 2022, UN experts said arbitrary arrests of Baha'is and the destruction or confiscation of their property bore all the signs of a policy of systematic persecution. Page blocks automated fetch; content confirmed from search listing.

title: Religion and Science
notes: Cited for: Draper (1874) and White (1896); the conflict model relies on Galileo's trial and Darwin's reception; most authors in the field see it as a shallow and partisan reading; Brooke's 1991 contextual history; Lemaitre proposed the Big Bang theory in 1927.

title: Galileo, Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina (1615), excerpt
notes: Cited for: Galileo quotes an eminent churchman that the Holy Spirit's intention is to teach how one goes to heaven, not how heaven goes.

title: Darwin and design
publisher: Darwin Correspondence Project, University of Cambridge
notes: Cited for: religious responses to Origin ranged from complete condemnation to active support; Kingsley's 'just as noble a conception of Deity', added to the second edition; Asa Gray, a devout Presbyterian, defended natural selection.

title: Georges Lemaitre
notes: Cited for: Belgian, ordained a priest in 1923; in 1927 proposed the theory that became the Big Bang.

title: Thomas Hertog, 'The Figure and Legacy of Monseigneur Georges Lemaitre'
notes: Cited for: at the 1958 Solvay conference Lemaitre called the model a scientific hypothesis entirely outside metaphysics or religion; he objected to Pius XII's 1951 address linking cosmology to creation.
